chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), regarding the statement of

Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Do you make the giving of drink to the pilgrims and the guarding of the Sacred Mosque like him who believes in Allah and the Last Day?' This was revealed regarding Hamza, Ali, Ja'far, al-Abbas, and Shu'ayb. Indeed, they prided themselves on the giving of drink and the guardianship. So Allah, Glorious and Mighty, revealed: 'Do you make the giving of drink to the pilgrims and the guarding of the Sacred Mosque like him who believes in Allah and the Last Day?' And it was Ali, Hamza, and Ja'far (may the prayers of Allah be upon them) who believed in Allah and the Last Day and fought in the way of Allah, and they are not equal in the sight of Allah.

key_terms.سِقَايَةَ الْحَاجِّ: Giving of drink to the pilgrims

ai.seo_question: Who were the people for whom the verse 'Do you make the giving of drink to the pilgrims...' was revealed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the specific occasion of revelation for Surah At-Tawbah 9:19, identifying the Prophet's uncles—Hamza, Ja'far, al-Abbas, and Shu'ayb—alongside Imam Ali (as) as the Quraysh leaders who boasted of their custodianship (Saqiya and Hijaba) of the Kaaba. It establishes a crucial Shia theological distinction: while these figures held prestigious ritual roles, the verse elevates those who combined true faith with active jihad, implicitly highlighting the superior spiritual status of Imam Ali and his brothers over mere administrative or ritual service. This narration underscores the Shia view that divine merit is rooted in spiritual conviction and struggle rather than lineage-based ritual privileges alone.
